newsitem.title: UK: P&O, Stena to merge Channel ferries.
newsitem.headline: P&O, Stena to merge Channel ferries.

text.p: Britain's P&O European Ferries and Stena Line AB of Sweden said on Thursday they would merge their short-sea ferry businesses on the English Channel into an operator with the same market share as the channel tunnel.

In a joint statement the two companies, whose profits have been squeezed by an intense price war with Eurotunnel for passengers and freight between France and England, said they would reduce capacity and costs. P&O will hold 60 percent of the shares in the new P&O Stena Line and Stena 40 percent.

"The new company will offer more vigorous competition to Eurotunnel and improved scheduling, as well as maintaining the present high standards on the existing ferry services and providing for eventual future investment," the companies said, adding it was the only way to match Eurotunnel.

The parent companies will contribute a total of 14 ships to the new group, which will have gross assets worth 410 million pounds ($642 million) and be "signficantly cash generative". They predict they can slash at least 75 million pounds off its initial fixed cost base of 280 million pounds.

While P&O puts in business and assets in return for the transfer of debt and liabilities amounting to 173 million pounds and 51 million pounds of cumlative preference shares, Stena Line will swap business and assets for debt of 134 million pounds. A definitive agreement for the establishment of the company is expected to be entered into before the end of November, though it will be subject to regulatory approval by national authorities and the European Commission.
